title: ci: three-way version coherence gate (pyproject / tag / PyPI)
body:
## What

Replaces the one-directional version-drift gate (WO-19 4.5) with a three-way coherence gate: `scripts/check_version_coherence.py` + `.github/workflows/version-coherence.yml` (PRs, pushes to main, and a **daily schedule** — a publish can fail silently after a tag is pushed, and no PR will exist to catch it). The old `version-drift.yml` is removed so exactly one version check remains.

## Assertions

| | scope | on failure |
|---|---|---|
| **A** `pyproject >= PyPI latest` | PRs + main | hard fail — the rollback check; message states the rule: *never lower a version to pass a check — bump forward instead* |
| **B** `newest release tag == PyPI latest` | main + daily | hard fail — everything tagged gets published, nothing published is untagged (the WO-19 defect class) |
| **C** `pyproject == newest tag` | main + daily | warn — legitimate mid-release state; escalates to hard fail once the bump commit is older than 7 days |

Comparisons use `packaging.version.Version`. Release tags are selected by pattern (`v<maj>.<min>.<patch>`) across all tags rather than git topology — this org carries foreign-namespace tags (`ts-sdk-v*`, `ts-types-v*`, `v1`, `*-integration`) and at least one release tag that is not an ancestor of main after a history rewrite. Repos with no tags or no PyPI release are treated as 0.0.0 with the relevant assertion skipped and noted.

## Why the old gate was insufficient

It only asked "does a tag exist for the pyproject version?" — a rollback trivially satisfies that (the *old* tag exists), which is exactly how the actenon-protocol 1.2.0 → 1.1.0 rollback passed. Both failure directions were demonstrated against the new gate before shipping (ASSERT A on a deliberately lowered version, ASSERT B on a deliberately unpublished tag).

title: fix: restore package version to 1.3.0 — never lower a version to pass a check
body:
## What

Corrects the version rollback introduced by #7, which lowered `pyproject.toml` from `1.2.0` to `1.1.0` while tag `v1.2.0` existed and PyPI served `1.2.0`. A source build from `main` produced an artifact stamped `1.1.0` that actually contained post-`1.2.0` code.

## Why 1.3.0, not 1.2.0

`main` carries substantive additive changes since `v1.2.0` (`git diff --stat v1.2.0..main -- . ':!pyproject.toml'`): the pre-compiled JSON refusal catalogue + compiler script, the extras restructure that made the zero-dependency claim true, expanded `refusal_codes.py`, and CI gates. Relabelling that tree `1.2.0` would be a second lie; the version moves **forward**.

## Root cause

#7's rationale was version coherence with `version.py` and the README badge — but those carry the **wire protocol** version (legitimately `1.1.0`), while `pyproject.toml` carries the **package** version (legitimately `1.2.0`). The two are now explicitly distinguished in `VERSIONING.md`, and the rollback is recorded in `FINDINGS.md`.

The one-directional version-drift gate could not catch this (a rollback satisfies "the pyproject version has a tag" because the *old* tag exists). A follow-up PR replaces it with a three-way coherence gate whose failure message names the rule: *never lower a version to pass a check — bump forward instead.*

## After merge

Tag `v1.3.0` on the merge commit → publish workflow → PyPI `1.3.0`, restoring `pyproject == newest tag == PyPI`.

Note: the existing version-drift check is expected to fail on this PR (tag `v1.3.0` cannot exist before merge). That transient state is exactly what the replacement gate downgrades to a warning.

title: Close doc-to-code drift: make "zero dependencies" claim true (Fable 5 Part 3A)
body:
## What

Closes the highest-priority finding from Fable 5 review Part 3A: the protocol README advertises `Zero dependencies` with a `Dependencies-0` badge, but `pyproject.toml` declares four runtime deps (`pydantic`, `jsonschema`, `rfc8785`, `pyyaml`).

For a trust product whose value proposition is *honest verifiable claims*, an unverifiable claim about itself is the worst kind of drift.

## What changed

### The claim is now TRUE, not removed

* `dependencies = []` in `pyproject.toml` (true zero-dep runtime)
* Optional extras:
  - `[types]` → pydantic (for `actenon_protocol.types`)
  - `[yaml]` → pyyaml (for direct YAML catalogue loading)
  - `[conformance]` → jsonschema + rfc8785 (for the conformance runner)
  - `[all]` → all of the above
  - `[dev]` → `[all]` + pytest, ruff, build

### Pre-compiled JSON catalogue

* `refusals/catalogue.v1.yaml` is now pre-compiled to a bundled JSON file (`python/actenon_protocol/data/catalogue.v1.json`) at build time
* `refusal_codes.py` loads JSON by default, falls back to YAML only when `[yaml]` is installed
* YAML remains the human-editable source of truth
* `scripts/compile_yaml_to_json.py` regenerates the JSON; `--check` for CI

### Version coherence

* `pyproject.toml` version: `1.2.0` → `1.1.0` (matching `version.py` and README badge)
* The previous `1.2.0` was unreachable from the package code

### Vector count drift

* CI step name said `117 vectors`; actual count and README claim is `129`
* Step renamed to `Run conformance suite (129 vectors)`

### `make verify-claims` gate

Machine-verifies every claim the README makes about the package itself:
* zero runtime deps (tomllib check)
* YAML↔JSON catalogue sync
* Python badge in sync with `requires-python`
* README install instructions valid
* Ecosystem table in sync with `ecosystem.yaml`

### New CI gates

* `Verify zero runtime dependencies` (lint job)
* `Verify YAML→JSON catalogue is in sync` (lint + conformance jobs)

## Verification

* Fresh venv with `pip install -e actenon-protocol` (no extras) imports cleanly with **zero** third-party packages installed:
  ```
  Installed distributions: [actenon-protocol, pip]
  pydantic:       NOT installed
  jsonschema:     NOT installed
  rfc8785:        NOT installed
  yaml:           NOT installed
  actenon_protocol version: 1.1.0
  canonicalize_json({"b":1,"a":2}) = {"a":2,"b":1}
  ```
* `conformance/python/`: 187 passed, 21 skipped with `[dev]` install
* `make verify-claims` passes
* `scripts/compile_yaml_to_json.py --check` passes

## What this does NOT do

* Does not remove the YAML file (still source of truth)
* Does not change any wire format or protocol version
* Does not change any conformance vector
* No breaking changes for callers using `pip install actenon-protocol[dev]` — the dev extra now pulls in `[all]` automatically

## Follow-ups (out of scope for this PR)

* Extend the same `verify-claims` pattern to kernel, permit, scan, cloud (separate PRs)
* Add the multi-language conformance matrix to CI (Part 3B)

Refs: Fable 5 review Part 3A (doc-to-code drift) and Part 3G (verify-claims gate).

title: feat(typescript): add @actenon/protocol runtime canonicaliser (WO-5)
body:
## WO-5 — Publish `@actenon/protocol` runtime canonicaliser

### What this PR ships

A new package `@actenon/protocol` under `typescript-runtime/` that provides compiled JS + `.d.ts` declarations for the ACTENON-JCS-STRICT-1 canonicaliser. The existing `@actenon/protocol-types` package ships `.ts` source only; this package ships compiled output importable by any JS/TS runtime (Node.js, Bun, browsers).

This is the prerequisite for WO-4a: the `@actenon/sdk` needs to `import { canonicalize } from "@actenon/protocol"` to verify `v2.` grant tokens signed with ACTENON-JCS-STRICT-1. Without this package, there is no TypeScript canonicaliser for the SDK to import.

### Files

- `typescript-runtime/src/canonicalisation.ts` — runtime implementation (adapted from the existing `typescript/src/canonicalisation.ts`, which was already correct but shipped as `.ts` source only)
- `typescript-runtime/src/index.ts` — public API: `canonicalize`, `canonicalizeBytes`, `canonicalizeJson`, `parseJson`, `CanonicalisationError`, plus re-exports from `@actenon/protocol-types`
- `typescript-runtime/tests/conformance.ts` — runs all 37 normative vectors + TS-specific adversarial tests
- `typescript-runtime/package.json` — `@actenon/protocol` 1.0.0, depends on `@actenon/protocol-types`, ships `dist/` + `src/`
- `typescript-runtime/tsconfig.json` — compiles to `dist/` with declarations
- `.github/workflows/publish-ts-runtime.yml` — npm publish with provenance (GitHub OIDC)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — new `typescript-runtime` CI job: typecheck + build + conformance + `npm pack --dry-run`
- `conformance/vectors/canonicalisation/invalid/deeply_nested_exceeds_limit.json` — fixed: was "Python-only" (no `input_json`), now language-neutral with literal 33-level nested JSON

### Conformance vector fix (WO-5 task 3)

The `deeply_nested_exceeds_limit.json` vector was annotated "Python-only" — it had no `input_json` field, just a note saying "In Python, the test constructs a 33-level nested dict." This is not language-neutral. **Chose option 1** from the WO: expressed the depth-limit test as literal JSON embedded in `input_json`. Any language's JSON parser can now parse it; the canonicaliser must reject it because depth 33 > 32.

### Acceptance criteria

1. **All 37 vectors pass** — 30 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed. Skips are JS-specific:
   - 2 valid vectors with integers > 2^53 (JS Number precision loss — callers must use BigInt)
   - 2 invalid vectors (`float_zero`, `float_exponent`) where JS `Number.isInteger(0.0)` returns `true` after JSON.parse
   - 8 invalid vectors without `input_json` (NaN/Infinity aren't valid JSON, so can't be parsed)
   
   5 extra TS-specific tests also pass: NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, BigInt, `canonicalize` returns `Uint8Array`.

2. **`npm pack` + `npm publish --dry-run`** — both succeed. Package is 6.6 kB, 11 files.

3. **Byte-parity** — Python and TS produce identical SHA-256 for `{"reason":"café — goodwill","n":1}`:
   ```
   Python: 7f397bbe16051b1652dabb7a9a515d3414801f8606599c3cf4be5a01710d1f4c
   TS:     7f397bbe16051b1652dabb7a9a515d3414801f8606599c3cf4be5a01710d1f4c
   ```

### npm provenance

The publish workflow uses `--provenance` (GitHub OIDC → npm trust) instead of a long-lived token. The `NPM_TOKEN_ACTENON` secret is still passed as a fallback until the `@actenon/protocol` package on npm is configured for keyless provenance at https://www.npmjs.com/package/@actenon/protocol/access. Once configured, the token can be removed.

### What's next

After this PR merges and `@actenon/protocol@1.0.0` is published to npm (via tag `ts-runtime-v1.0.0`), WO-4a becomes unblocked:
1. SDK 1.5.0 imports `canonicalize` from `@actenon/protocol` and accepts both `v1.`/`v2.` token prefixes
2. Permit switches `str(d.normalize())` → `format(d.normalize(), 'f')` for readable decimals
3. Permit adds `ACTENON_TOKEN_VERSION=1` escape hatch
4. Permit release notes state minimum SDK version requirement

title: feat(docs): render ecosystem table from ecosystem.yaml
body:
## WO-2 — single source of truth for the ecosystem table

The ecosystem table was hand-copied into four repo READMEs plus the org profile README, and the copies had already diverged. This PR makes `actenon-protocol` the canonical source and renders the table everywhere else from it.

### What this PR ships

- `ecosystem.yaml` at the repo root — the single source of truth
- `python/actenon_protocol/ecosystem.py` — the renderer, shipped inside the package so `pip install actenon-protocol` gets it with no network access at runtime
- `python/actenon_protocol/data/ecosystem.yaml` — the YAML bundled as package data (covered by the existing `data/*.yaml` glob)
- README wrapped with `<!-- ECOSYSTEM-TABLE:START -->` / `<!-- ECOSYSTEM-TABLE:END -->` markers, existing hand-written table replaced with the rendered form
- `ci.yml` adds an `ecosystem table in sync` step to the lint job
- `Makefile` adds an `ecosystem` target
- Version bumped 1.1.0 → 1.2.0 (new tool shipped inside the package; semver minor). `PROTOCOL_VERSION` in `version.py` is unchanged — no wire-format change.

### Renderer CLI contract

```
python -m actenon_protocol.ecosystem --check README.md --repo <name>   # exit 1 on drift
python -m actenon_protocol.ecosystem --write README.md --repo <name>
```

`--repo` is REQUIRED. The renderer does not auto-detect the current repo from `git remote get-url origin`: detection works locally and fails silently under fork checkouts, detached HEAD, and custom remotes, putting the `← you are here` marker on the wrong row with nobody noticing. Explicit beats clever.

### Output shape (between the markers)

1. The four repo rows as a markdown table, row matching `--repo` marked `← you are here`
2. A blank line
3. The `**Optional:**` line, with the cloud licence string (`source-available; see its LICENSE`) that WO-11 just shipped to `actenon-cloud/main/README.md`

The `Not required by any component above; every capability in this ecosystem works without it.` clause is load-bearing: WO-9's `test_cloud_optional.py` makes it machine-checkable, so it must be present verbatim in all four READMEs — which is precisely why it is generated rather than hand-copied.

`actenon-cloud` stays PUBLIC but stays OUT of the table rows. It appears only in the `Optional` line beneath the rows.

### Sequential dependency (WO-2 §7)

This PR merges AND publishes to PyPI first. The three consumer PRs (kernel, permit, scan) wait until `pip download actenon-protocol==1.2.0` resolves, because their `--check` CI step does `pip install actenon-protocol`.

### Not in scope

- actenon-cloud stays out of the table rows (per WO-2 §3)
- The renderer is a BUILD and CI concern; it must never become a runtime import of any other package
- No vendored copies of the renderer into consumer repos; no fetch-and-exec from a URL. Consumers get it via `pip install actenon-protocol`

title: Canonicalisation cross-language conformance (Phase 5)
body:
## Summary

Makes canonicalisation a single, documented cross-language invariant across Protocol, Kernel, Permit, Cloud SDK code and fixtures. Fully specifies `ACTENON-JCS-STRICT-1` with all 18 required behaviours, adds 37 normative conformance vectors (22 valid + 15 invalid), and provides a reusable conformance command for each repository.

## Normative profile

**`ACTENON-JCS-STRICT-1`** (profile version 1) — retained, fully specified.

## All 18 behaviours explicitly defined

| # | Behaviour | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Object key ordering | UTF-8 byte order, ascending (RFC 8785 §3.2.3) |
| 2 | UTF-8 | All output UTF-8; non-ASCII NOT \u-escaped |
| 3 | Unicode normalisation | None — caller's responsibility |
| 4 | Strings | RFC 8259 escaping; literal non-ASCII |
| 5 | Integers | Decimal, no leading zeros, no + sign, arbitrary precision |
| 6 | Negative integers | `-` prefix + absolute value |
| 7 | Zero | Always `0` |
| 8 | Booleans | `true` / `false` |
| 9 | Null | `null` |
| 10 | Arrays | Order preserved, no whitespace |
| 11 | Nested objects | Recursive key sorting |
| 12 | Duplicate keys | Prohibited — parser's responsibility |
| 13 | Unsupported numbers | Decimal, complex — rejected |
| 14 | Floating-point | REJECTED (the defining STRICT characteristic) |
| 15 | NaN and Infinity | REJECTED (not valid JSON) |
| 16 | Dates and timestamps | String or integer, no special handling |
| 17 | Binary values | Base64url string, no special handling |
| 18 | Absent vs null | Absent = not in output; null = `"key":null` in output |

## Canonical byte examples

```
{"z":1,"a":"hello","b":[true,null,42]}
→ {"a":"hello","b":[true,null,42],"z":1}

{"é":1,"Z":2,"a":3}
→ {"Z":2,"a":3,"é":1}

[1,2,3] → [1,2,3]
[3,2,1] → [3,2,1]  (arrays preserve order)

{"present":1,"null_field":null}
→ {"null_field":null,"present":1}

{"present":1}  (absent field)
→ {"present":1}
```

## Digest algorithm

SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the canonicalised JSON. Output: 64-character lowercase hex string.

## Prohibited inputs

Floats (including NaN, Infinity, -Infinity), non-string dict keys, sets, bytes, custom objects, `undefined` (JS), input deeper than 32 levels, canonical output exceeding 1 MiB.

## Adversarial test results

| Test | Python | TypeScript |
|---|---|---|
| Reordered keys | ✅ same bytes | ✅ same bytes |
| Unicode edge cases | ✅ correct | ✅ correct |
| Visually similar strings (Latin/Cyrillic/Greek A) | ✅ distinct bytes | ✅ distinct bytes |
| Duplicate keys | ✅ documented (parser responsibility) | ✅ documented |
| Integer boundary values (int32/int53/int64) | ✅ correct | ⏭️ skip (>2^53 precision loss) |
| Float injection | ✅ rejected | ✅ rejected |
| Exponent notation | ✅ rejected | ⏭️ skip (JS Number ambiguity) |
| NaN | ✅ rejected | ✅ rejected |
| Infinity | ✅ rejected | ✅ rejected |
| Deeply nested (30 valid / 33 invalid) | ✅ correct | ✅ correct |
| Oversized (>1 MiB) | ✅ rejected | ✅ rejected |
| Alternate whitespace | ✅ ignored (parser handles) | ✅ ignored |
| Escaped vs unescaped equivalent | ✅ same bytes | ✅ same bytes |
| Omitted fields | ✅ absent from output | ✅ absent from output |
| Null substitution | ✅ `"key":null` in output | ✅ `"key":null` in output |
| Array reordering | ✅ different bytes | ✅ different bytes |
| Unicode normalisation (precomposed vs decomposed) | ✅ different bytes | ✅ different bytes |

## Python result

- Conformance suite: **108 passed, 21 skipped** (Python-only vectors)
- Conformance CLI: **39 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped**

## TypeScript result

- Conformance: **28 passed, 0 failed, 13 skipped**
- Typecheck: **0 errors**
- Unit tests: **21 passed, 0 failed**

Skips are JS-specific limitations (integers >2^53 lose precision in JS Number; `0.0` and `1.5e10` parse as integers in JS). These are documented in the spec and the conformance runner.

## Compatibility handling

- `ACTENON-JCS-STRICT-1` retained as canonical label (no change).
- `RFC8785-JCS` retained as deprecated alias (backward verification).
- `actenon-jcs-sha256-v1` rejected (never accepted).
- No canonical bytes changed — existing proofs continue to verify.
- New vectors are additive (no existing vector modified in a way that changes expected bytes).

## Summary

Initial release of `actenon-protocol` v1.0.0 — the neutral, open, implementation-independent boundary contract for the Actenon ecosystem. This PR lands the wire-format source of truth, the canonicalisation profile, the refusal-code catalogue, the identifier registry, the execution-mode definitions, the conformance vectors, and the Python + TypeScript reference types.

This PR is the formal review gate for the v1.0.0 release. Merging it tags `v1.0.0` and publishes the protocol.

---

## What this repository IS

`actenon-protocol` is the **wire contract** for consequential-action execution. It defines the artefacts that cross the trust boundary between an authority broker (such as `actenon-permit`) and a protected resource (verified by `actenon-kernel` or any compatible verifier).

It owns:
- Protocol versioning
- Identifier formats and prefixes
- Execution modes (`brokered`, `resource_owned`)
- Proof claim names
- Refusal codes
- Verification outcome codes
- Execution outcome codes
- Canonicalisation profile identifiers
- `ExecutionProof`
- `ExecutionReceipt`
- `ExecutionRefusal`
- Trusted issuer metadata
- Evidence-linkage fields
- Conformance test vectors
- Generated Python types
- Generated TypeScript types
- OpenAPI-compatible schema components

## What this repository is NOT

It is **not** a fifth commercial product. It does NOT own:
- Policy evaluation, approvals, budgets, tenant models, credential storage, provider adapters, Cloud persistence, billing, the complete hosted `AuthorisedExecutionIntent` lifecycle, action execution.

## Refusal taxonomy

20 canonical refusal codes in 6 categories, with a two-layer disclosure model:
- **Public-safe** (`disclosed_code`, always present): 14 umbrella codes (`MALFORMED_REQUEST`, `UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION`, `CANONICALISATION_FAILURE`, `PROOF_MISSING`, `PROOF_INVALID`, `PROOF_EXPIRED`, `PROOF_NOT_YET_VALID`, `REPLAY_DETECTED`, `AUTHORITY_REVOKED`, `POLICY_REFUSAL`, `CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE`, `PROVIDER_REFUSAL`, `PROVIDER_FAILURE`, `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`).
- **Detailed** (`internal_code`, trusted-only): 6 detail codes that collapse to `PROOF_INVALID` under public policy (`ISSUER_UNTRUSTED`, `SIGNATURE_INVALID`, `AUDIENCE_MISMATCH`, `TARGET_MISMATCH`, `ACTION_MISMATCH`, `PARAMETER_MISMATCH`).
- **Compatibility aliases**: 21 existing Kernel/Permit `FailureCode` strings preserved as aliases (e.g. `PCCB_REQUIRED`→`PROOF_MISSING`, `DUPLICATE_REPLAY`→`REPLAY_DETECTED`, `INTENT_MISMATCH`→`PARAMETER_MISMATCH`, `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`→`POLICY_REFUSAL`).

## Compatibility decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Adopt `ACTENON-JCS-STRICT-1` as canonical label | Matches Kernel HEAD (`actenon/proof/canonical.py:20`). Audit K-01 found three labels in flight; this resolves the drift. |
| Accept `RFC8785-JCS` as deprecated alias | Historical proofs in the wild carry this label; rejecting them would break deployments. |
| Reject `actenon-jcs-sha256-v1` | Doc-only label; no implementation accepted it. Removes a drift vector. |
| Preserve all 16 existing `FailureCode` enum members as aliases | No rename required in Kernel/Permit/Cloud. |
| Preserve `grant_`, `intent_`, `act_` prefixes | In active use; changing would break existing tokens. |
| Add `proof_`, `exec_`, `rcpt_`, `rful_`, `authz_` as new canonical prefixes | Artefacts that previously had no canonical prefix on the wire. |
| Make `execution_mode` an explicit required field on every artefact | Audit P-01/C-04 found its absence allowed trust-boundary collapse. |
| Two-layer disclosure model (`disclosed_code` + `internal_code`) | Audit C-01 found Cloud tests pinned to `SIGNATURE_INVALID` while Kernel emits `PROOF_INVALID` in public mode; making disclosure explicit on the wire resolves this. |
| Separate `proof_id` (replay key) from `exec_` (idempotency key) | Audit K-04 found Kernel conflates replay with idempotency. |
| Floats rejected in canonicalisation | Matches Kernel behaviour; floats produce non-deterministic bytes across languages. |

## What this PR adds on top of the initial release commit

The initial release commit (`87a87b8`) landed the protocol itself on `main`. This PR (`release/v1.0.0` → `main`) adds two governance/documentation files to give reviewers a concrete reviewable surface and downstream maintainers an adoption roadmap:

1. **`INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md`** — phased adoption plan (Phase A: Kernel, B: Permit, C: Cloud, D: Scan) with file-level change forecasts for each repo, referencing audit findings from the programme-level audit report.
2. **`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`** — reviewer checklist enforcing protocol-impact classification, conformance, compatibility, and documentation requirements per `VERSIONING.md` and `GOVERNANCE.md`.

No wire-format changes. No conformance vector changes. No breaking changes.

---

## Unresolved questions (documented in CHANGELOG.md)

1. **Replay-store contract** — protocol defines `REPLAY_DETECTED` but not the replay-store API. Currently treated as an implementation concern.
2. **Idempotency key** — `execution_attempt_id` is introduced as the idempotency key (separate from `proof_id`), but not yet tested across implementations.
3. **Issuer-status discovery** — `issuer_metadata` well-known URL pattern (`/.well-known/actenon-issuer/<issuer_id>`) is proposed but not conformance-tested. Deferred to v1.1.
4. **Multi-issuer proofs** — current schema assumes single issuer per proof. UCAN-style delegation chains may require multi-issuer support. Deferred to v1.1.
5. **Cross-language conformance runner** — current suite is Python-only. A TypeScript port is planned for v1.1 to prove byte-identical canonicalisation across languages.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Wire format is the source of truth (`schemas/*.v1.json`), not the markdown
- [ ] No policy/approval/budget/tenant/credential/adapter/persistence concerns introduced into the protocol repo
- [ ] `execution_mode` is explicit on every artefact (no inference from deployment location)
- [ ] Disclosure policy preserved: `SIGNATURE_INVALID` etc. never appear as `disclosed_code` under public policy
- [ ] All existing `FailureCode` enum members preserved as compatibility aliases
- [ ] `ACTENON-JCS-STRICT-1` is the canonical canonicalisation label; `RFC8785-JCS` is a deprecated alias; `actenon-jcs-sha256-v1` is rejected
- [ ] Conformance suite passes (90 Python + 21 TypeScript)
- [ ] `INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md` accurately reflects the audit findings and the phased adoption plan
